title: prefill-decode-stage-overlap-chunked-speculative-kernel-scheduler-kvcache-optimizations
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: Reduce end-to-end latency and increase throughput for mixed prefill+decode workloads by overlapping prefill and decode stages, adding chunked speculative prefill, improving kernel scheduling heuristics, and making KV cache access non-blocking under continuous batching. This PR implements: 1) chunked prefill path that breaks long prefill sequences into prefill(->KV) chunks enabling early decode overlap; 2) speculative prefill attempts for likely-next-token prefixes to warm KV and attention kernels; 3) a lightweight kernel scheduler that prioritizes critical-path decode kernels and dynamically reorders prefill work when decode latency SLOs are at risk; 4) non-blocking KV cache read path and lock-free per-shard KV prefetch to avoid stalls during high-concurrency workloads. Changes are conservatively gated behind runtime flags and rollout config with telemetry to monitor model-quality regressions. Summary of measured improvements on internal perf-canary against 7B/13B mixes: median latency for interactive burst workloads down 9-12%, p95 latency down 18%, and throughput (tokens/sec) up ~22% under mixed prefill+decode traffic with continuous batching enabled. Checklist: - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf bench harness updates - [x] feature flag gating - [x] canary rollout plan - [x] docs + release notes. Related: ENG-18234, ENG-18300, PRs: pr-87111 (kv-cache-refactor), pr-86147 (kernel-scheduling-proto).
